questions.prompt: Which metadata must follow a source into every retrievable chunk?
options: Tenant, ACL, source/version/locator, digest, lifecycle, and processing versions
questions.explanation: Chunk-level provenance and policy metadata make authorization, freshness, deletion, reproduction, and citation verification enforceable.

questions.prompt: Why should ACL and lifecycle filtering happen before sparse, vector, and reranking stages?
options: It prevents unauthorized or stale evidence from entering candidate scoring and downstream context
It removes the need for identity
questions.explanation: Post-filtering can leak candidates and scores, waste capacity, reduce recall, or expose restricted text to later ranking and generation components.

questions.prompt: Which query is the strongest reason to preserve a lexical BM25-style branch?
options: An exact policy identifier such as UW-17
questions.explanation: Sparse retrieval is especially valuable for exact identifiers, rare names, codes, numbers, and terminology that dense representations can blur.

questions.prompt: What does reciprocal rank fusion avoid assuming?
options: That raw sparse and dense scores share a calibrated scale
questions.explanation: RRF combines rank positions rather than incomparable raw score magnitudes, making it a useful hybrid baseline before calibrated score fusion.

questions.prompt: A newly uploaded version is flagged as poisoned. What is the safest default?
options: Publish it because it is newest
Quarantine it without silently replacing the known-good active version
questions.explanation: Version recency does not establish safety or authority; quarantine keeps suspect content out while an explicit recovery workflow proceeds.

questions.prompt: What should happen when an ingestion operation ID is retried with different content?
options: Treat it as an operation conflict
questions.explanation: A stable operation ID represents one exact intent, so changed payload under the same ID must not produce a different knowledge state.

questions.prompt: A generated citation ID exists in the corpus but was not retrieved for this request. What should the application do?
options: Reject it as a forged citation
Ask the model whether it is allowed
Add it to the retrieved set after generation
questions.explanation: Existence does not prove request-scoped retrieval, authorization, currency, or support; citations must be bound to validated evidence for this request.

questions.prompt: Why revalidate cited evidence after generation?
options: To close the race where evidence is deleted, superseded, or unauthorized after retrieval
To replace the source of truth
questions.explanation: Retrieval is a time-of-check; citation validation must confirm that the evidence remains unchanged, current, and authorized at publication time.

questions.prompt: What is the denominator of Recall@k?
options: All labelled relevant evidence for the evaluated cases
questions.explanation: Recall@k measures how much of the labelled relevant set appears in the top-k results; incomplete relevance judgments can bias it.

questions.prompt: Why can metadata filtering reduce approximate-nearest-neighbour recall?
options: The search budget may visit neighbours later removed by the filter
questions.explanation: Filtered candidates can consume a bounded ANN exploration budget, requiring filter-aware indexes, iterative scans, partitioning, or tuned exact fallbacks.

questions.prompt: When is GraphRAG justified over an established hybrid baseline?
options: Whenever a graph library is available
When measured global or relational questions benefit enough to justify extraction and operating cost
questions.explanation: Graph construction adds derived data, lineage, quality, deletion, latency, and cost concerns and should solve a measured query class.

questions.prompt: What security property does a source embedding provide?
options: Neither; embeddings remain sensitive derived data
questions.explanation: Embeddings can leak source information and must inherit access, encryption, retention, query, and deletion controls from the source data.
